candidates.excerpt: Each maker advertises a per-CJ fee policy `(cjfee_a, cjfee_r)`. Within a single round the realized maker fees are a deterministic function of each policy and the equal-output amount, and because policies in the live JoinMarket network are diverse, those realized fee values are typically *unique within the CJ*: no other slot in the round would have charged the same fee at the same amount. That uniqueness lets a passive on-chain observer attribute each equal output to a specific maker slot whenever it is reused in a downstream CJ. The signal is in the block; no network-level mitigation reduces it.
